findings.title: snort-full reader signed f_msg_size underflow yields strncat stack overflow.
findings.description: read_snortfull tracks remaining space in a signed int f_msg_size. After a first [**] [ line of length >= 6105, f_msg_size drops below 40. The preprocessor/date branch then calls strncat(f_msg, ++q, f_msg_size - 40) with a negative length, which becomes a huge size_t and overflows the stack buffer f_msg[OS_MAXSTR+1]. Classification/Priority paths can similarly drive f_msg_size negative before the third-line strncat.
findings.impact: Crash or likely code execution in ossec-logcollector whenever snort-full localfile monitoring is enabled and an attacker can write the monitored file (or influence Snort to emit a long first line plus a date-shaped follow-up).
findings.attack_path:
1. Operator configures <localfile><log_format>snort-full</log_format><location>PATH</location></localfile>.
2. Attacker writes PATH with a >=6105-byte line starting with [**] [ and a second line matching MM/DD-... with a space.
3. logcollector read_snortfull subtracts into a negative f_msg_size and strncat overflows f_msg.
4. Process crashes or attacker-controlled stack corruption runs as the logcollector user.
findings.remediation: Use size_t for remaining capacity; abort the event (or truncate safely) when remaining < bytes to append; never pass (f_msg_size - N) when f_msg_size < N.
findings.poc_video_notes: Built a minimal two-line PoC log demonstrating f_msg_size=38 then strncat n=-2. No live logcollector was crashed in this at-rest environment.

findings.title: doDiff joins unsanitized syslog hostname into /queue/diff path, enabling chroot write escape.
findings.description: When lf->hostname does not start with '(', doDiff snprintfs DIFF_DIR/hostname/sigid/last-entry. hostname_map allows '/'. Stock rule 533 check_diff matches ossec: output: 'netstat -tan, and the ossec decoder prematches ^ossec: , so a syslog UDP/TCP event with a traversal hostname and that body triggers _add2last mkdir/fopen/fwrite outside /queue/diff under the analysisd chroot.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated (when syslog remote + allowips permits the source) write of attacker log bytes to attacker-chosen directories under the OSSEC chroot as ossecr. Basename is fixed as last-entry under <sigid>/.
findings.attack_path:
1. Operator enables remoted connection syslog with allowips including the attacker (or uses the already-reported dotted-quad netmask ACL bypass).
2. Attacker sends syslog: '<pri>Mon DD HH:MM:SS ../../tmp/pwn ossec: output: 'netstat -tan': crafted\n'.
3. analysisd decodes as ossec, rule 533 check_diff runs doDiff.
4. File /tmp/pwn/533/last-entry (in chroot) is created with attacker content.
findings.remediation: Sanitize hostname for path use (reject '/', '..', and non-allowlisted bytes) or hash/encode it before joining under DIFF_DIR.
findings.poc_video_notes: Validated by tracing syslog CleanMSG hostname assignment into doDiff path join and _add2last mkdir/fwrite. Default configs use secure-only remote, so syslog must be enabled.
